title: Cyclone blew the clothes off boys — Sherman Daily Democrat 'Look through Sherman's past' retrospective
text:
Cyclone blew the clothes off boys

Files of Sherman Daily Democrat,
June 1, 1937
(Compiled by Ann Lowry)

SAVOY — Fifty-seven years ago May 28, a cyclone struck Savoy, and moved the town. The freakish wind demolished every house on Main Street and the town was rebuilt on Hayes Street which is now Highway 82.

Not a single resident who witnessed the cyclone remains in Savoy, but several in this area can tell of the storm. H.H. Arterberry, merchant here for 40 years, but now lives southeast of town, recalls a Miss Minnie McMurray who was blown from her home into a pen some distance away.

Dr. S.D. Moore of Van Alstyne and his former roommate, Sam Harle of Durant, Okla., were blown two blocks from their bedroom and every thread of their clothing went with the wind.

Cows were found with their feathers.

Thirteen were killed in the cyclone and the old Halsell College was turned into an emergency hospital.

Look through Sherman's past

THIRTY YEARS AGO
June 1, 1957

John W. Bailey, 518 Belden, who has served 47 years with the MK&T Railroad as agent of the Sherman freight and passenger office since 1930, retired from active duty in May.

TWENTY YEARS AGO
June 1, 1967

Staff photo— Students at Van Alstyne High School have named their youth center "The Shack." The name is proving to be inaccurate since the center will contain almost $2,000 worth of equipment when completed. Community fund raising projects and donations have made the center possible. Standing in front of the facility is Mike Bradley, president of the Van Alstyne Youth Council.

TEN YEARS AGO
June 1, 1977

FARMERSVILLE — Clifford Carpenter, long-time civic and business leader, will be honored with his own day June 25 by the Farmersville Rotary Club.

Mayor G.R. Brandon, in a proclamation making June 25 "Clifford Carpenter Day," said the honor is based on "the many contributions he has made for the betterment of our community."
notes: This article from June 1, 1977 reprints and expands on a June 1, 1937 Sherman Daily Democrat account of the Savoy cyclone, which struck May 28 (fifty-seven years before 1937 = 1880). The Savoy cyclone section is the primary Savoy-relevant content. The 'Look through Sherman's past' section contains three 'years ago' retrospectives (30, 20, 10 years) from 1957, 1967, and 1977 respectively, which are unrelated to Savoy. The famous line 'Cows were found with their feathers' appears to be a garbled/humorous corruption in the original text (likely meant 'Chickens were found plucked' or similar). The article was compiled by Ann Lowry. The cyclone demolished every house on Main Street; town was rebuilt on Hayes Street (now Highway 82). Thirteen killed; Halsell College used as emergency hospital.
